items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Then I go down south with Billy Fowler's band

ctx.x: So that was at that period. Now, that's the late period. That's in the Sixties, before I come down here.

All right. So I go with Danny Love(?). We go to Baltimore and we play a couple of towns. Then I go down south with Billy Fowler's band, which is a band. We get stranded in North Carolina, and I'm around there. We stayed around there about four or five weeks, a little longer. We went there anticipating that somebody is going to book us around there. We through all that part of the country. When we get down there, there's quite a few bands around

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Played with Luis Russell’s band and Billy Fowler’s band.

ctx.x: I’m there. I’m around. I around where all the action is, so they be seeing me. I’m around. I’m sharp, neat. Always I’m like that, because you dress up every day, and I like that. Dress up. Collar and tie, and you go out. The bars that you hang out in, and the joints you hang in, there are always chorus girls around, show chicks. You’re young and you’re smart and you want to be a man. You see these women, stacked up, little waist, hips like a horse, and they all there, and you’re there, so you want to be sharp,…

“Lucky Millinder’s looking for a guitar player. He’s breaking up the Blue Rhythm Band. It’s going to be Lucky Millinder and his Cotton Club Orchestra. No more Blue Rhythm Band.” Did I tell you why the Blue Rhythm Band was founded?
